title: Challenge: install, upgrade, and roll back with Helm
intro: Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes: install a chart as a named 'release', upgrade it, and, when an upgrade goes wrong, roll it back instantly. Let's run that lifecycle. (Commands checked; output illustrative.)

steps.instruction: Install the ./chart as a release named 'my-api'.
steps.success:
NAME: my-api
LAST DEPLOYED: now
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1

steps.instruction: List your Helm releases to see it.
steps.success:
NAME     NAMESPACE  REVISION  STATUS    CHART
my-api   default    1         deployed  api-0.1.0

steps.instruction: Ship a change: upgrade 'my-api' to 3 replicas (override the value).
steps.success:
Release "my-api" has been upgraded. Happy Helming!
REVISION: 2

steps.instruction: That upgrade broke things. Roll 'my-api' back to revision 1.
steps.success: Rollback was a success! Happy Helming!  (now on revision 3, identical to revision 1)

done: Solved! install → list → upgrade → rollback → uninstall. Helm tracks every release revision, so an upgrade is never a one-way door, `helm rollback` makes recovering instant.
